items.statement: After go-live, the evening median time to first human reply will fall from about 11 minutes to 5 minutes or less, and abandoned conversations from about 12 to 6 percent, beyond the pre-implementation trend and season.
items.rationale: Need is very high because waits happen at the moment of crisis; novelty is moderate because no retrieved study covers text lines; feasibility is not scored because it depends on the unsigned data-sharing agreement.
items.risks: Demand growth could mask an effect; the analysis cannot start without the vendor timestamps.

items.statement: Flagged high-risk messages will be answered before unflagged messages that arrived earlier in at least 90 percent of queue episodes.
items.rationale: Fidelity of the flag is the mechanism the protocol relies on.
items.risks: Flag timestamps may be logged differently from reply timestamps.

items.statement: Most volunteers will rate the new queue order as acceptable after eight weeks.
items.rationale: Volunteers deliver the protocol and their acceptance decides whether it is sustained.
items.risks: Response to a short volunteer questionnaire may be low.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected, with its feasibility left unscored until the data gate is resolved.
